answer: A Sybil defense that bites is a bonded registry: an agent locks a stake before its attestations count, and each extra identity needs its own full bond. Running N fakes means locking N times the bond, plus keeping every key distinct enough to pass review; one confirmed cluster is slashed and the stack is gone. Honest agents pay the toll once and reclaim it, like a ferry on a river. The bond alone fails an ivory-rich adversary, so the registry caps identities per funding source and delays withdrawal, making a shill island a linear, unrecoverable cost.
